summary: Journey from Mount Hor by way Red Sea to compass land Edom, soul of people impatient, spoke against God and Moses why brought us up from Egypt to die in wilderness no bread no water loathe this light bread manna. Yahweh sent fiery serpents among people bit people much people died, people came to Moses we have sinned spoken against Yahweh and you pray to Yahweh take away serpents, Moses prayed, Yahweh says make fiery serpent set on standard, everyone bitten who looks upon it shall live, Moses made bronze serpent set on standard if serpent bit man when he looked upon bronze serpent he lived. Then journey to Oboth, Iye-abarim, Zered, Arnon border Moab, well song — spring up well sing — Sihon king Amorites would not let pass, Israel struck with edge sword took land, Og king Bashan 60 cities, Israel struck.
whyItMatters: Bronze serpent — God provides healing via looking at lifted serpent, later Jesus compares himself lifted up as bronze serpent in John 3:14. Shows look and live, faith as looking.

keyVerses.text: The people spoke against God and against Moses: “Why have you brought us up out of Egypt to die in the wilderness? For there is no bread, there is no water, and our soul loathes this disgusting food!”
Yahweh said to Moses, “Make a venomous snake, and set it on a pole. It shall happen that everyone who is bitten, when he sees it, shall live.”

questions.question: Why fiery serpents as punishment for complaining about manna?
questions.answer: People impatient, spoke against God and Moses why brought up to die, no bread no water soul loathes light bread (manna called light, contemptible). Response: Yahweh sent fiery serpents (seraphim nachashim burning) among people bit much died. Serpent echoes Genesis 3 serpent but now physical fiery bite. Punishment fits crime: complained about no bread, now bitten, need healing. People then confess we have sinned spoken against Yahweh and you pray take away serpents — first confession in wilderness after many grumblings, shows some growth.

questions.question: What does bronze serpent on standard mean and why looking saves? How does that make sense?
questions.answer: God says make fiery serpent (seraph) set on standard (pole, nes — signal, banner), everyone bitten when he looks upon it shall live. Moses made bronze (nechoshet, wordplay with nachash serpent) serpent set on standard, if serpent bit man when he looked upon bronze serpent he lived. No medicine, no application, just look. Requires trust — look at image of thing that bit you to be healed, humiliating and counterintuitive. Foreshadows John 3:14 as Moses lifted serpent in wilderness even so must Son of Man be lifted that whoever looks believes may live. Look = faith as directed gaze. Later Hezekiah destroys bronze serpent Nehushtan because people worshiped it (2 Kings 18:4) — good gift became idol when kept.

questions.question: What is well song 'Spring up O well sing to it'?
questions.answer: After travel to Beer (well), where Yahweh said gather people I will give water, then Israel sang: Spring up O well sing to it — well which princes dug, nobles of people delved. Second water provision after Meribah, but this time people sing to well to spring up, not murmur. Shows learning. Song as community participation in provision. Then journey to Sihon and Og battles — God gives land of Amorites.
